children: The president of Japan's Chubu Electric Power
is expected to resign after the firm was found to have submitted falsified seismic data in its application to restart the Hamaoka nuclear power plant, the Nikkei newspaper reported on Sunday.
Chubu will withdraw its application to restart two nuclear reactors at the plant, the paper reported on Friday.

Chubu's Hamaoka plant, in central Japan, had been undergoing a safety review in an effort to restart its nuclear reactors. Japan's nuclear watchdog had suspended a review following the data scandal and on Monday, Chubu released the regulator's investigatory report into the matter.
The incident could derail Japan's efforts to resume operation of its nuclear reactors, all 54 of which were suspended in the wake of the 2011 Fukushima earthquake and tsunami.
Earlier this year, Tokyo Electric Power restarted its reactor at Kashiwazaki-Kariwa, the world's biggest nuclear power plant.

The resignations of Chubu Electric President Kingo Hayashi and Chairman Satoru Katsuno are expected to be announced on Monday; Minoru Yasui, who is currently a director, will become president, the Nikkei said.

Separately, Chubu said last month that it had altered documents submitted to Japan's nuclear decommissioning fund manager in relation to the No. 1 and No. 2 plants at the Hamaoka site, which are currently being dismantled.
